forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: No change from yesterday's 21%. June 2026 discourse continues to cluster lab-insider AGI timelines around 2027-2030 (Amodei: powerful AI late-2026/2027; Hassabis: ~50% by 2030; Altman: within this presidential term), but none meets the resolution bar of a credible lab formally declaring AGI achieved or 3+ leading researchers stating so. Bar remains unmet.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: near-term insider predictions of a transformative technology arriving inside a fixed ~3.5-year window, where insiders carry strong optimism incentives. Such forecasts historically resolve YES well under half the time; base ~15-20%.

factors_up.factor: Lab leadership timelines (Amodei 2027, Hassabis ~50% by 2030) sit partly inside the window
Continued capability and capital momentum; OpenAI confidential S-1 filed 8 June signals sustained scale-up

factors_down.factor: Resolution bar (clean credible declaration or 3+ researchers) remains unmet and definitionally contested
Persistent generality/agentic shortfalls make a 'declared AGI' event before 2030 unlikely

key_uncertainties: Whether any major lab will formally use the term 'AGI' in a declaration rather than avoiding it
Whether 3+ leading researchers would publicly converge on 'AGI achieved'
update_triggers: Revise UP if a credible lab announces AGI or 3+ leading researchers state it is achieved
Revise DOWN if frontier progress visibly plateaus or labs explicitly disavow near-term AGI

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged up 1pp to 26%. Fresh reporting confirms McKinsey's ~10% (3,000-4,000 role) cuts — its largest since 2008 — explicitly tied to AI compressing research and analysis hours, with Bain, BCG and Deloitte slowing hiring or trimming headcount and utilisation sagging. Trend is accelerating, but a ≥33% revenue/employment decline primarily attributed to AI by end-2030 remains a high bar.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: incumbent professional-services sectors facing a major technology shock losing ≥a third of value/jobs within ~6 years. Historically rare; sectors tend to restructure and reprice rather than contract a third that fast. Base ~10-20%.

factors_up.factor: Concrete, AI-attributed layoffs now spreading across MBB and Big Four; utilisation falling
Value shifting from advisory headcount toward AI-augmented implementation, squeezing pyramid economics

factors_down.factor: 33% is a steep threshold; firms repricing/restructuring rather than collapsing
Demand for integrated strategy-tech-execution still growing (Accenture/Deloitte ~11-12%)
Attribution problem: separating AI effect from cyclical budget cuts by 2 credible analyses is hard

key_uncertainties: Whether headcount/revenue declines reach a full third by end-2030 versus plateauing in the teens
Whether credible analyses will attribute declines primarily to AI rather than the macro cycle
update_triggers: Revise UP if multiple major firms report double-digit revenue declines explicitly attributed to AI
Revise DOWN if consulting revenue stabilises or AI tooling becomes a net revenue driver

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: No change at 5%. Mid-June polling keeps Labour around 19% (PollCheck 7-poll average ~18.7%), running third behind Reform UK (~27%) and level with the Conservatives. With an election not due until 2029 there is time to recover, but the current position is dire and consistent with recent weeks.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: governing parties polling ~third place at mid-term recovering to win most seats at the next election. Mid-term recoveries happen, but recovering from third (≈8pp behind the leader) to plurality is uncommon; base ~15-25%, lowered by FPTP vote-splitting dynamics.

factors_up.factor: ~3 years of runway to the expected 2029 election allows mean reversion
Incumbency/organisational advantages and a fragmented right could yield seats on low vote share under FPTP

factors_down.factor: Labour third in polls (~19%) and roughly 8pp behind Reform
Reform's durable lead and a competitive Conservative party crowd the field

key_uncertainties: Whether Reform's lead proves durable or is a mid-term protest spike
How FPTP translates a fragmented vote into seats
update_triggers: Revise UP if Labour returns to within a few points of the lead or regains first place
Revise DOWN if Reform's lead widens further or Labour slips clearly into fourth

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: No change at 81%. The longer ~8.5-year window comfortably encompasses the clustered insider timelines (2027-2030) plus substantial slack for the resolution bar to be met. June discourse reinforces, rather than alters, this view.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: arrival of a long-anticipated general-purpose technology within a ~decade once leading developers forecast it within a few years. Such longer-horizon arrivals resolve YES more often than tight near-term ones; base ~55-70%.

factors_up.factor: Window spans well beyond the 2027-2030 cluster of insider timelines
Sustained compute, capital and research-automation momentum

factors_down.factor: Definitional/resolution ambiguity could delay a recognised 'AGI achieved' event even if capabilities arrive
Possible scaling plateaus or capital pullbacks over a decade

key_uncertainties: Whether a recognised AGI declaration occurs even if capabilities are broadly present
Whether scaling/algorithmic progress sustains or stalls over the decade
update_triggers: Revise UP if labs declare AGI or researchers broadly converge on it
Revise DOWN if progress plateaus through the late 2020s

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: No change at 8%. Mid-June saw a PRC 'maritime law enforcement' operation east of Taiwan asserting jurisdiction, but this stays well below the resolution threshold (blockade >72hrs or assault on Taiwan proper). US assessments (March 2026) find no fixed timeline and view amphibious operations as extremely difficult; markets price ~99.6% no invasion by mid-2026.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: great-power initiation of a major blockade or amphibious assault against a defended territory within a ~3.5-year window absent detectable mobilisation. Historically rare; base ~5-12%.

factors_up.factor: Sustained grey-zone pressure (incursions, law-enforcement ops, simulated blockades) keeps escalation risk live
2027 PLA capability milestone falls inside the window

factors_down.factor: No detectable large-scale amphibious or blockade mobilisation
High costs, US-intervention risk, and Beijing's stated preference for coercion short of war

key_uncertainties: Whether grey-zone coercion escalates into a sustained (>72hr) blockade
How the cross-strait and US deterrence picture evolves toward 2027-2029
update_triggers: Revise UP on detectable mobilisation, declared quarantine/blockade, or major escalation
Revise DOWN if cross-strait tensions ease or deterrence visibly strengthens

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged down 1pp to 5%. ONS data released 17 June shows May 2026 CPI at 2.6%, up from 2.5% in April — inflation is drifting up, not toward target. With only about six monthly prints left before 1 Jan 2027 and the rate well above 2.0% and rising, a sub-2.0% reading in the window looks increasingly unlikely.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: monthly CPI annual rate dropping more than 0.6pp below its current level within ~6 months absent a demand shock. Uncommon over such a short window; base ~10-15%.

factors_up.factor: Possible energy/base effects or a sharp demand slowdown could pull a single print down
Only one qualifying month needed, not a sustained fall

factors_down.factor: Latest print 2.6% and rising, leaving little time to reach <2.0% before 2027
Sticky services inflation and limited disinflationary momentum

key_uncertainties: Whether energy/base effects produce a one-off dip in any remaining 2026 print
The trajectory of services and core inflation through autumn 2026
update_triggers: Revise UP if a print drops sharply toward 2.0% or a clear disinflation trend emerges
Revise DOWN if inflation continues drifting above 2.5-3%

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged up 1pp to 83%. With a 31 July release and record-breaking presales (biggest US presales in five years; second-biggest first-day post-COVID presales after No Way Home) tracking a $200M+ domestic opening, the runway to $1.5B looks strong. No Way Home cleared $1.9B; the main risk is the high absolute bar plus China/legs uncertainty.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: marquee MCU/Spider-Man tentpoles with elite presales reaching $1.5B worldwide. A meaningful minority of top superhero films clear $1.5B; base ~40-55%, raised sharply by this title's franchise pedigree and presales.

factors_up.factor: Record presales and $200M+ opening tracking; direct No Way Home ($1.9B) lineage
Five-month runway (Aug-Dec) and strong summer/holiday legs potential

factors_down.factor: $1.5B worldwide is a high absolute bar only a handful of films reach annually
China performance and post-opening multiplier remain uncertain

key_uncertainties: Opening-weekend magnitude and the worldwide multiplier/legs
update_triggers: Revise UP on a record-breaking opening weekend and strong holds
Revise DOWN on a soft opening or weak international/China numbers

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: No change at 98%. Recent reporting puts OpenAI's run-rate near $25B and Anthropic's around $30B (April 2026), a combined ~$55B with steep month-on-month growth. Reaching a combined >$70B by Q4 2026 requires only modest continuation of current trajectories.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: paired hyper-growth software firms sustaining run-rate growth to clear a combined threshold ~27% above current levels within ~8 months. Given recent monthly step-ups, base is very high; ~90%+.

factors_up.factor: Combined run-rate already ~$55B and growing rapidly month-on-month
Strong enterprise demand and continued capital/scale-up (OpenAI S-1 filing)

factors_down.factor: Definitional risk in how 'ARR' is reported by credible outlets at Q4 2026
Possible growth deceleration or demand shock

key_uncertainties: Exactly how Q4 2026 ARR is reported/measured by credible outlets
Whether either firm's growth materially decelerates in H2 2026
update_triggers: Revise UP if either firm reports another large run-rate step-up
Revise DOWN if reporting shows a sharp slowdown or revenue restatement

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: No change at 39%. The OBR's March 2026 outlook puts medium-term potential output growth at 1.5% (with GDP averaging ~1.6% across 2027-2030 as the output gap closes). With the central estimate sitting essentially on the 1.5% threshold and ageing-population/productivity headwinds into the 2030s, exceeding 1.5% on a full-decade average is roughly a sub-coin-flip.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: UK realised decade-average real GDP growth exceeding 1.5%. The 2010s averaged ~1.5-2%; the 2020s have been weaker. Base ~40-50%, trimmed for structural headwinds.

factors_up.factor: OBR central potential output growth at 1.5% with productivity projected to recover toward 1.0%
Possible AI-driven productivity upside over a full decade

factors_down.factor: Ageing population and slowing labour-supply growth (~0.5%) weigh on potential
Threshold is 'exceed' 1.5% while the central forecast sits right at 1.5%
Long-horizon downside/shock risk over 2030-2039

key_uncertainties: Whether productivity growth recovers to or above OBR's central path
Realised labour supply and migration trends through the 2030s
update_triggers: Revise UP if productivity/AI gains lift potential output forecasts above 1.5%
Revise DOWN if OBR/independent forecasts downgrade 2030s potential growth
